div.head: Cn 1027 17
div.ab: Haec et his similia si, dum venero, non erunt persoluta, regia exactio secundum leges in quem culpa cadit, districte absque venia comparabit. Valete.

If, when I come, these and other similar dues have not been paid, they shall be exacted by the royal officials in accordance with the laws, sternly and without remission, from him who is found to be in fault. [Farewell.]

If these dues, and others like them, have not been paid in full when I come, the royal collectors are to obtain them according to the laws, sternly and without remission, from him who is in fault. Farewell.
div.note: Latin only (Cnut's letter of 1027, c. May; Latin translation c. 1070–1100, the Old English original is lost). Liebermann's text is from Florence of Worcester (ed. MGH SS XIII 126), compared with Ox (Oxford, Corpus 157 p. 329) and William of Malmesbury II 183; text in column T. Liebermann gives no German translation.
